title: On the triviality of the unramified Iwasawa modules of the maximal multiple $ mathbb{Z} p$-extensions

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states: 'Let k be a non-Galois CM-field of degree 4 or a totally imaginary cyclic extension over Q of degree 4... Then it is known that Δ ≃ Z/4Z (if k is cyclic) or D8 (if k is non-Galois).' This dichotomy omits the well-known third possibility for quartic CM fields: a biquadratic (Klein four, V4) CM field that is itself Galois over Q with Gal(k/Q) ≅ (Z/2Z)² (e.g., k = Q(i,√2)). Such fields are neither 'cyclic' nor 'non-Galois', so they are not covered by the two cases treated in Section 3, yet the paper's abstract and Theorem 1.1.1 claim a complete classification of degree-4 CM fields satisfying the hypotheses. No justification is given elsewhere in the paper for why this case can be omitted, making the 'complete classification' claim for [k:Q]=4 incomplete/unsupported as stated.
